title: U.S. House · Minnesota's 8th District
area: Northeastern Minnesota, including Duluth, the Iron Range, and the Boundary Waters region.

context.text: Incumbent Pete Stauber (R) won the August 11, 2026 Republican primary with 86.4% of the vote against Anthony Hamilton. Trina Swanson won the Democratic primary with 76.8% against Luke Gulbranson and John Munter.

candidates.name: Pete Stauber
candidates.ballotNote: Won the August 11, 2026 Republican primary with 86.4% of the vote.
candidates.currentRole: U.S. Representative (since 2019); Chair, Energy and Mineral Resources Subcommittee

summary.text: Stauber is the incumbent U.S. Representative for Minnesota's 8th District, first elected in 2018. He chairs the Energy and Mineral Resources Subcommittee of the Committee on Natural Resources and also serves on the Committee on Small Business and the Committee on Transportation and Infrastructure.

background.text: Born in Duluth, Minnesota, in 1966; earned a bachelor's degree in criminology from Lake Superior State University in 1986.
Previous work experience included playing professional hockey and serving as a police officer.
Served on the Hermantown city council (2001-2005 and 2011-2013) and the St. Louis County Board of Commissioners (2013-2019).

priorities.text: Chairs the Energy and Mineral Resources Subcommittee of the Committee on Natural Resources, focused on mining and energy development in the Iron Range.
Serves on the Committee on Transportation and Infrastructure and the Committee on Small Business, including the Rural Development, Energy, and Supply Chains subcommittee.

record.text: Chairs the Energy and Mineral Resources Subcommittee of the Committee on Natural Resources in the 119th Congress (2025-2026), a role he has held since the 118th Congress.

Serves on the Committee on Small Business (Rural Development, Energy, and Supply Chains subcommittee) and the Committee on Transportation and Infrastructure (Aviation; Highways and Transit; Railroads, Pipelines and Hazardous Materials subcommittees) in the 119th Congress.
Served as ranking member of the Energy and Mineral Resources Subcommittee during the 117th Congress (2021-2022), before Republicans held the House majority.

candidates.name: Trina Swanson
candidates.ballotNote: Won the August 11, 2026 Democratic primary with 76.8% of the vote.

summary.text: Swanson is a former federal immigration official from the Duluth area running as the Democratic nominee against incumbent Pete Stauber, campaigning on affordability, government accountability, and rural community investment.

background.text: Grew up in Duluth and Hermantown, graduating from Hermantown High School; earned degrees from the University of St. Thomas and Mitchell Hamline School of Law.

Spent 25 years in federal government service, beginning at the Bankruptcy Court at age 18, then working for U.S. Citizenship and Immigration Services running immigration operations in three countries.
Says she left her federal career rather than compromise her oath, and returned to northern Minnesota to run for Congress.
background.quote: I walked away from that career rather than compromise my oath.

priorities.text: Affordability: lowering prescription drug prices, expanding rural health care access, protecting Medicare and Social Security, and supporting jobs in mining, manufacturing, and the skilled trades.
priorities.quote: Affordability is my top priority. I will focus on lowering prescription drug prices, expanding rural health care access, protecting Medicare and Social Security, strengthening domestic supply chains, and supporting good-paying jobs in mining, manufacturing, and the skilled trades.

priorities.text: Government stability and accountability, including opposing stock ownership or trading by members of Congress.
priorities.quote: Congresspeople should not be allowed to hold or trade stock when in office.

priorities.text: Community presence, including in-person town halls in every county, infrastructure investment, and responsible mineral extraction that protects the Boundary Waters Canoe Area Wilderness.
priorities.quote: investing in infrastructure, supporting responsible extraction of critical minerals while protecting the environment, protecting the BWCA

positions.summary: Supports lowering prescription drug prices and expanding rural health care access.
positions.quote: I will focus on lowering prescription drug prices, expanding rural health care access, protecting Medicare and Social Security

positions.summary: Supports 'responsible immigration reform that protects our borders while upholding our values,' without specifying enforcement or deportation policy.
positions.quote: ensuring responsible immigration reform that protects our borders while upholding our values
